column3: These are is not separately expressed.
What is repeated three times without an explicit shall I say.
Ways is the second object rather than vigor; the final expression concerns wiping out kings without explicitly naming people who ruin them.
The last phrase contains where with strong drink rather than an explicit verb crave.
The drinker is singular, and the final action changes the cause of all sons of affliction.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Those defended are literally sons of passing away rather than specifically dispossessed.
Close to the Hebrew.
The woman is of ability or valor, and her price is explicitly compared with precious coral.
Trust is expressed as completed, and the gain is called spoil rather than anything of value.
Doing him good is expressed as completed.
Seeking and working are expressed as completed actions.
She has been like ships of a merchant; her food is specifically bread.
Rising and giving are completed finite actions rather than an infinitive of providing.
She considered and took the field, without a separate verb buy; she planted from the fruit of her palms.
She girded her loins and strengthened her arms rather than showing them to be strong.
The perception of gain is expressed as completed.
The second pair is palms rather than fingers; the actions are completed.
Her palm is singular in the first clause rather than plural arms; spreading and stretching are completed.
Close to the Hebrew.
The coverings are made for herself, without explicitly naming a bed, and making is completed.
Gates is plural.
Belt and merchant are singular, and making, selling, and supplying are expressed as completed.
She laughed at the latter day, with a singular day and no explicit can.
Opening her mouth is expressed as completed.
Close to the Hebrew.
Her sons rose and called her blessed, and her husband praised her; the actions are completed.
You have risen above them all is expressed as completed.
Beauty is called vanity, and the woman will be praised.
